title: Build the messages the server sends on its own

blocks.text: Besides answering, your server now starts messages of its own on the link to each terminal: echoes, notices that it is about to sign off for maintenance, and short texts for the merchant (an 0620 with the text in field 63). `LinkMessages` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/LinkMessages.java` keeps one template per kind, and the methods that build each kind are written.

The operations team reports two problems from the pilot. A terminal displayed a maintenance window it had never been sent, the one added to the previous notice. And the terminals' logs show an echo and a merchant text from the server in flight at the same time with the same STAN.

Finish the two methods marked `TODO`: `fromTemplate` and `nextStan`. The constructor receives the last STAN the server used on the link, so numbering carries on across restarts, and a clock that a test can fix. About six lines in total.

cases.says: an echo and a merchant text carry their template's fields, a six-digit STAN and a send time, and pack
two messages of one kind take consecutive numbers after the last one used
a field added to one message never appears in the next, and building the next never changes the first
echoes, notices and merchant texts draw their STANs from one sequence for the link
after 999999 the sequence starts again at 000001, never 000000
field 7 is the send time in GMT, whatever zone the server's clock is in

origin.section: 2.6 A Message the Server Starts Is a Fresh Copy, Numbered by the Server

concepts: A message the server starts is a fresh copy of its template, numbered from the server's one sequence for the link and stamped with the time in GMT.
